subsection: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
question_text: Why did the United States enter the Korean War?

official_answers.text: To stop the spread of communism

why_it_matters.text: After WWII, Korea was split into a communist North (backed by USSR and China) and an American-backed South. In 1950, North Korea invaded the South. The U.S. led a UN coalition to defend South Korea. About 36,000 Americans died over 3 years. The war ended where it began: with Korea divided at the 38th parallel.

fun_fact.text: The Korean War (1950-53) ended with an armistice — not a peace treaty. North and South Korea are still technically at war today. The war split one Korean nation into two opposite worlds: South Korea became a thriving democracy and major economy with companies like Samsung, and the K-pop music industry. North Korea is one of the most isolated countries on Earth.
